Shadow Priest Rotation in 

Shadow Priest operates on a single resource system with a single hard-hitting spender. The rotation generally adheres a basic priority and a few overarching principles with several moving parts and short cooldown abilities to keep track of. AoE is much of the same, except you deal damage to targets evenly by cleaving off a single priority target using Tentacle Slam and Psychic Link . Shadow's rotation can be boiled down to the following. 

 

 

 
 Maximise Shadow Word: Madness Uptime Insanity is Shadow's only resource which it uses to cast Shadow Word: Madness . Prioritize using Shadow Word: Madness to keep your insanity from capping at 100. Keeping Shadow Word: Madness up for as long as possible will increase your damage through Mastery: Shadow Weaving . 
 

 

 
 

 
 Keep Cooldowns on Cooldown: Alongside a resource system, Shadow has a variety of short, medium, and long duration cooldowns to manage. The rule of thumb is to prioritize shorter cooldown spells over longer cooldown spells to avoid situations where you lose an overall use of an ability throughout an encounter. 
 

 

 
 
 
 React to Procs: Shadow has several procs like Shadowy Insight , and Mind Devourer which need to be reacted to and spent as and when they occur to avoid wasting potential spell casts.

 Best Shadow Priest Opener

 The Shadow Priest Opener has some small deviations depending on your Hero Talent. Each opener is underpinned by three core goals, put the most important spells on cooldown, generate Insanity to start maintaining Shadow Word: Madness , and react where needed to any important procs that occur throughout the first 10 to 15 seconds. Pre-Combat Check

 Before any combat happens, it is important for Shadow Priests to make sure the following are done. This applies to raids, dungeons, delves, or even open-world content.

 Shadow Priest Major Cooldowns

Shadow Priest has two to three major cooldowns, depending on which Hero Talent you choose to use. 

 
 Power Infusion 

 Due to the talent Twins of the Sun Priestess , Power Infusion can be cast on allies in order to provide them with the same buff to haste that you provide to yourself when you activate it. This means as a Shadow Priest you should be aiming to find a target for Power Infusion who is going to consistently get high value from the haste buff every 2 minutes. In some cases, you can even change your Power Infusion targets throughout the encounter or dungeon, as well as time your cooldowns around those of your allies to get the maximum benefit. However, you should always prioritize your own value and damage from Power Infusion over that of others. Make sure you are always getting the maximum number of uses possible, and timing it with your other powerful cooldowns. 

 
 Voidform 

 

 Voidform is an unusual cooldown compared to most as very little of its value comes from the damage bonuses associated with having the Voidform buff, and instead it comes from having access to the new spell, Void Volley . Void Volley is a spell that Shadow Priests aim to prioritize during Voidform so as not to potentially lose a cast throughout its duration.

Voidform can also be extended as Archon through the Sustained Potency talent, as well as the Ancient Madness talent. 

Shadow Priests should use Voidform on cooldown as consistently as possible, as this will result in it lining up perfectly with Power Infusion , Halo , and Void Torrent .
 

 
 Halo 

 Halo is the keystone cooldown of the Archon Hero Talent. This ability gains value by dealing some AoE direct damage, as well as by generating resources and procs through the Manifested Power and Sustained Potency talents. This ability triggers over a long period of time due to Power Surge , Energy Conservation , and Divine Halo . This slow ramp up means you should ideally use this cooldown early on in your opener and future cooldown sequences to avoid spending time in cooldowns waiting for Halo to generate procs or deal damage.
